issues.description: DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT duplicated rather than referenced from canonical source
issues.detail: The constant DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT = 16 is now declared locally in Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat instead of being statically imported from Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat. Two copies of the same on-disk magic number is a silent-drift hazard: if the core constant ever changes, the legacy reader will mis-decode existing indexes with no compile-time warning. Either keep the static import from the canonical home, or add an explicit invariant comment tying the two values together.

issues.description: fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of expressing read-only-ness in the type system
issues.detail: Both legacy formats override fieldsWriter to unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException, which is an LSP violation against KnnVectorsFormat's contract that promises a usable writer. The read-only constraint should be lifted into the type system (a ReadOnlyKnnVectorsFormat base, a marker interface, or fail-fast at codec construction) rather than communicated by a runtime exception reached only after a flush attempt. As written, callers discover the misuse via NPE-equivalents in production.

issues.description: numMergeWorkers and mergeExec constructor parameters are accepted, validated, then silently discarded
issues.detail: Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat's constructor still accepts numMergeWorkers and mergeExec, validates them, but the fields were removed and fieldsWriter throws anyway. The signature advertises behavior the object no longer provides; callers passing real executors will believe they configured something they did not. Either remove the parameters (and the validation) or document loudly that they are accepted only for source compatibility and have no effect.

issues.description: @Deprecated annotation stripped at exactly the lifecycle moment it should be most informative
issues.detail: Both Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat lost their @Deprecated annotation in the move to backward_codecs. Users still referencing the old fully-qualified name during migration now get a runtime UnsupportedOperationException on write instead of a compile-time deprecation warning. Restore @Deprecated (or a since-tagged variant) so the compiler and IDEs can warn callers who still construct the legacy format directly.

issues.description: Protected fields on OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues demoted to package-private while class remains public abstract
issues.detail: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues's previously protected fields (dimension, size, scalarQuantizer, slice, byteBuffer, etc.) are now package-private, but the class is still public abstract with public subclasses. External subclasses that previously extended this class can no longer access these fields, silently tightening the subclassing contract. Either keep them protected, or make the class non-public/sealed so the new visibility is provably safe.

issues.description: Public NAME constants demoted to package-private — potential downstream compile break
issues.detail: Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.NAME and Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.NAME were public static final String constants and are now package-private. External tooling, integration tests, and downstream consumers (Elasticsearch, OpenSearch) that reference these by name will fail to compile. Either keep the constants public (optionally @Deprecated), or document explicitly why the narrowing is safe with a migration note.

issues.description: Test-only RW subclasses re-enable writing by extending a type whose stated contract forbids it
issues.detail: Lucene99RWScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and Lucene99RWV1HnswScalarQuantizationVectorsFormat extend the read-only legacy formats solely to override fieldsWriter and put writing back. This is inheritance-for-reuse working around the supertype's invariant, and it forced visibility downgrades (e.g., rawVectorFormat from private to package-private) on production code purely to serve test scaffolding. A composition-based writer factory would honor the contract without subclassing a type whose contract explicitly forbids writing.

issues.description: PR ships multiple concerns in one diff with author-acknowledged incomplete work
issues.detail: The diff combines a mechanical move, API visibility narrowing, writer disabling, and test-scaffolding refactor into a single patch, while the author admits Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorScorer cannot easily be moved yet. Splitting into mechanical-move, API-deprecation, and writer-disable patches would make each piece reviewable on its own merits. Land the parts that are complete with a clear scope rather than merging a half-move where the scorer is stuck in core but the format is in backward_codecs.

issues.description: Two RW test formats (V0 and V1) with overlapping names and no central documentation of the taxonomy
issues.detail: Lucene99RWHnswScalarQuantizationVectorsFormat is renamed to V0, and a new V1 is added; the only hint is a one-line javadoc. State explicitly what V0 and V1 correspond to (pre-versioning writer vs writer with VERSION_ADD_BITS) in a package-info comment or class javadoc, with the file format version constants referenced, so the next contributor doesn't add a V2 without understanding the shape.

issues.description: rawVectorFormat field widened from private to package-private to accommodate test-tree writer subclass
issues.detail: Production code's encapsulation was loosened specifically so Lucene99RWScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat in the test tree can reach in. Either inject the dependency through a protected accessor with a documented contract, or accept that this class is now part of the testable surface and document it. The widening reads as incidental but is load-bearing for the test fixtures; that asymmetry should be stated.

issues.description: Read-only-after-rotation policy communicated only by exception string, not as documented invariant
issues.detail: The contract 'Old codecs may only be used for reading' is asserted at runtime via UnsupportedOperationException on two distinct classes, with no class-level javadoc or marker interface stating the invariant. Add a literate paragraph at each class javadoc explaining that the format is retained for reading segments produced by Lucene 9.9, that writing is intentionally unsupported, and that test-only writer subclasses live in the test source set. Consider a ReadOnlyVectorsFormat marker if this pattern will repeat for future format rotations.

issues.description: VERSION_START / VERSION_ADD_BITS / VERSION_CURRENT lack on-disk semantic comments
issues.detail: The format keeps VERSION_START = 0, VERSION_ADD_BITS = 1, VERSION_CURRENT = VERSION_ADD_BITS as bare integers. For a legacy format whose entire purpose now is to be read correctly across versions, each transition should state what actually changed on disk. Otherwise an engineer debugging a corrupted segment has to git-archaeology their way to the answer.

issues.description: Writer logic moved into test tree without clarifying bw-compat index generation story
issues.detail: Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsWriter is moved to backward-codecs src/test, meaning the only path to write the legacy format now lives in test source. If bw-compat index generation tooling needs to produce a legacy index outside the test classpath, it cannot. State explicitly whether bw-compat index generation lives in tests; if not, this is the wrong shape.

issues.description: Module boundary leak: backward_codecs still depends on evolving core lucene99 classes
issues.detail: The legacy format in backward_codecs still imports Lucene99HnswVectorsFormat, Lucene99HnswVectorsReader, and Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat from core. The intended contract of backward_codecs is 'read-only support for old on-disk formats, isolated from the evolving core', but this PR leaves the legacy reader tethered to live core classes that may themselves evolve. Decide which side owns these classes and draw the boundary cleanly; otherwise a future core refactor will silently break legacy reads.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a mechanically sound move of the Lucene99 scalar-quantized formats into backward_codecs, but the read-only-after-rotation story is unfinished and the patch bundles too many concerns. The most consistent concerns across reviewers: DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT is silently duplicated rather than referenced (drift hazard), fieldsWriter throwing UnsupportedOperationException expresses a read-only invariant via runtime exception instead of the type system (LSP violation), and constructor parameters (numMergeWorkers/mergeExec) are accepted and validated but silently ignored. Several silent API narrowings compound the picture: @Deprecated stripped at exactly the moment it carries the most signal, public NAME constants demoted to package-private (potential downstream compile break), and protected fields on a public abstract OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues demoted to package-private. Test-only RW subclasses reach into production internals through visibility downgrades, indicating composition rather than inheritance would have been cleaner. Recommend splitting the diff, restoring @Deprecated, preserving public API surface where downstream depends on it, and either centralizing the block-shift constant or asserting the invariant explicitly before merge.
